claims.nodeLabel: 3I/ATLAS interstellar object and the US government response (November 2025)
claims.text: The episode exposed the absence of a standing government scientific body able to speak to anomalous objects, the gap the UAP Science Advisory Council was announced across seven months later. Reasoning: the same scientist, Loeb, was the principal public voice in both episodes.

claims.nodeLabel: AARO invite-only UAP research workshop (early August 2025)
claims.text: The workshop is the operational precursor to the June 2026 UAP Science Advisory Council. Reasoning: same subject matter (standardising UAP data capture and analysis), same sponsoring office, and an overlapping population of independent researchers, ten months apart.
'Since UAPs are physical objects that interact with humans, the council includes members with expertise in physical sciences as well as psychology and biology.'
'The goal of the council is to advise the U.S. government on how to resolve the nature of UAP.'
Named a member of the UAP Science Advisory Council announced 17 June 2026.
The UAP Science Advisory Council reports to the UAP Governance Board, whose mission includes optimising interagency processes to ensure more effective support to AARO.

No charter, membership roster or meeting record for the UAP Governance Board is public as of 12 August 2026. Reasoning: it is named only in derivative reporting about the Science Advisory Council and appears on no AARO or war.gov page.
A 12-member UAP Science Advisory Council chaired by Avi Loeb was announced on 17 June 2026 to advise an interagency UAP Governance Board including ODNI, FBI and DoW.

Avi Loeb formed and leads the UAP Science Advisory Council, announced June 2026; named members include Carol Cleland, Richard Cloete, Omer Eldadi, Tim Gallaudet, Ross Howard, Ben Lamm, Devesh Nandal, Garry Nolan, Michael Shermer, Peter Skafish, Matthew Szydagis and Jennice Vilhauer.
The council reports to the UAP Governance Board, which supports AARO and whose mission includes optimising interagency processes to 'ensure more effective support to' AARO.

The council is the institutional locus where PURSUE's unassessed imagery and AARO's unpublished assessments could be joined; no published product exists as of 12 August 2026. Reasoning: the two programmes have complementary gaps and the council is the only body chartered across both.
